critical_findings.finding: Data-leakage prevention is underspecified and could fail in real note collections: the plan introduces a mandatory privacy guard (publish:false or configurable equivalent), but the underlying convention is not confirmed (capsule A2/A3; open Q2) and the canonical risk register still has K8 mitigation=null. Failure mode: notes the user intended as private are emitted as HTML and/or included in the search index and then hosted publicly (static-only, no access control).

closure.closure_target: M1/DL6 + update risk register entry K8 to include mitigation, owner, and testable acceptance; require explicit configured privacy convention(s) and default-safe behavior.

critical_findings.finding: Privacy guard can be bypassed indirectly if "private" notes are loaded into the shared build context and processed by downstream plugins before exclusion is enforced. Failure modes: (a) private content leaks into search index (R7/R8) or tag/link pages generated by other plugins, (b) private titles/excerpts leak via build summaries/warnings/logs, (c) plugin authors forget to honor the privacy flag consistently because exclusion is not a first-class invariant of C10 APIs.

closure.closure_target: Make publishability a core invariant in Shared Build Context (C10): private notes must be excluded from all query APIs by default; enforce at ingestion time and re-check at emit/search-index time; add explicit tests that assert private content is absent from (1) emitted HTML, (2) search index artifacts, (3) tag/backlink pages, (4) build reports/logs.
closure.evidence: plan_candidate_B2B_v1:/plan_package/architecture/chosen/high_level_dataflow (all plugins consume C10); plan_candidate_B2B_v1:/plan_package/milestones/0/deliverables/1 (DL2 shared context APIs); plan_candidate_B2B_v1:/plan_package/milestones/4/deliverables/0 (DL24 search index plugin); requirements_canonical_v1:/requirements/6 (R7 client-side search); requirements_canonical_v1:/requirements/7 (R8 search index artifact).

critical_findings.finding: Site output can become an XSS delivery vehicle when notes are shared publicly: Markdown rendering + templating + possible theme overrides risks unsafe HTML/JS injection. Even with "raw HTML disabled by default", gaps remain if templates interpolate unescaped metadata (titles/tags), if sanitization is incomplete, or if theme customization allows script injection (K7, K19). Failure mode: a crafted note (or copied snippet) executes JS in readers' browsers, exfiltrating data from the static site origin.

closure.closure_target: Define and enforce a strict output-encoding/sanitization policy across BOTH Markdown render plugin (C14) and template/theme plugin (C15): escape all metadata fields; sanitize rendered HTML; explicitly prohibit arbitrary JS injection via theming in v1 (or require explicit opt-in + warnings). Add security regression fixtures for known payloads in Markdown body, front matter, tags, and titles.

critical_findings.finding: Link resolution rules are likely to be wrong for the user's corpus because Q1 (link conventions) is blocking/unconfirmed, yet the plan commits to relative links + optional wiki-links with precedence. Failure mode: links resolve to the wrong note (especially with duplicate titles/slugs), backlinks become incorrect, and navigation trust is lost; worse, “helpful” auto-resolution may silently mis-link content.

closure.closure_target: Before implementing C13, obtain a confirmed answer for Q1 and codify resolver precedence + disambiguation UX (warnings/errors). Add fixtures for ambiguous cases (duplicate titles, relative path variants, anchors) and require deterministic resolution outputs.

critical_findings.finding: Build performance and resource usage can fail catastrophically because target scale (Q3) is blocking/unconfirmed, yet the chosen architecture assumes shared in-memory context across plugins. Failure mode: builds hang/crash on large note sets or large individual files; search indexing and Markdown rendering become bottlenecks; user cannot complete a build (violating R6) and may lose trust in outputs.

closure.closure_target: Confirm Q3 early and translate to explicit build-time and memory budgets; design C10 and plugin APIs to allow streaming/chunking where feasible; add stress fixtures and progress logging; define "fail fast" thresholds and partial-build behavior.

critical_findings.finding: Non-deterministic output is likely in a plugin-based build unless ordering and stable iteration are enforced from day one. Failure modes: filesystem traversal order differences (OS/filesystem), plugin ordering changes, and non-sorted tag/link collections produce noisy diffs and inconsistent URLs/backlinks/search index. This can break deployments and make bugs hard to reproduce (K20).

closure.closure_target: Specify deterministic ordering requirements in the plugin API (DL3) and enforce in core engine (C9) + shared context (C10): sorted note IDs, stable tag ordering, stable output paths; prohibit timestamps unless explicitly enabled; add deterministic-build tests earlier than M6 if possible.

critical_findings.finding: Malformed YAML front matter (K6) has no defined mitigation and can crash the pipeline or silently drop metadata. Failure modes: build fails (violating R6) or tags/pages are incomplete/misleading; worst case, a single bad note blocks the entire build.

closure.closure_target: Define strict-but-tolerant front-matter parsing behavior: per-file errors become warnings by default with file context; optionally configurable strict mode to fail CI; add fixtures for common YAML errors and encoding edge cases.
closure.evidence: risk_gov_canonical_v1:/risk_register/5 (K6 mitigation null); plan_candidate_B2B_v1:/plan_package/synthesis_warnings/1 (W2 notes missing K6 mitigation); requirements_canonical_v1:/requirements/5 (R6 actionable errors).

critical_findings.finding: Cross-platform path + slug/output-path handling can corrupt site integrity: Windows path separators, Unicode normalization, case-insensitive filesystems, and reserved filenames can cause (a) incorrect link resolution, (b) output overwrites/slug collisions, (c) broken asset URLs on deployment targets. This can manifest as missing pages and incorrect backlinks/tags/search.

closure.closure_target: Define canonical note identifiers and output paths (prefer path-based IDs), implement slug collision detection as a hard error or prominent warning, normalize Unicode and case consistently, and add OS-matrix tests for path edge cases (including duplicate names differing only by case).

critical_findings.finding: A user misconfigures or misunderstands the privacy guard for notes containing sensitive information. The build process does not fail loudly, resulting in the inadvertent publication of private content to a public server when the user deploys the static output.

closure.closure_target: The privacy guard must be designed with safety-critical UX, such as requiring an explicit override flag to publish, printing unmissable warnings for skipped files, or generating a manifest of published vs. private content for user review.

critical_findings.finding: The build process, reliant on a purely in-memory shared context, consumes excessive RAM when processing a large collection of notes (e.g., >10,000), causing the process to crash or hang. This renders the tool unusable for power users and fails to meet scalability requirements.

closure.closure_target: The Shared Build Context API (C10) must be designed to handle large scale, potentially by using a disk-backed store or streaming data access patterns instead of holding the entire note graph in memory. Stress tests must validate performance at the upper bound of expected scale.

critical_findings.finding: A user includes a legitimate but vulnerable JavaScript snippet within a note. The build process includes this active content without sufficient sandboxing, creating a stored XSS vulnerability in the generated site that could be exploited by other page content or a malicious link.

closure.closure_target: HTML sanitization must be enabled by default and difficult to disable. If scripts are allowed, the build output must include a strict Content Security Policy (CSP) to sandbox their execution. The build must warn when raw script tags are encountered.

critical_findings.finding: Two plugins operate on the same data during the same lifecycle hook (e.g., modifying tags) but have conflicting logic. Due to implicit or incorrect execution order, one plugin silently corrupts the data needed by the other, leading to an incorrect but successfully built site that the user may not immediately notice is broken.

closure.closure_target: The plugin API must provide explicit controls for execution order (e.g., 'runs_after'). The core engine should support schema validation or data integrity checks between plugin executions in a debug mode to detect such conflicts.

critical_findings.finding: A user performs a large-scale refactoring of their notes (e.g., renaming a directory), breaking hundreds of relative links. The build process only emits warnings and generates a site with dead links, providing no tooling to assist the user in fixing the links in the source files, leading to a frustrating and error-prone manual recovery.

closure.earliest_prevention_stage: M3 (Link Resolution, Backlinks & Tag Extraction Plugins)
closure.closure_target: The tool must provide a utility beyond simple warnings, such as a structured broken-link report for scripting or a semi-automated refactoring command to help users update links in their source Markdown files after file moves.

critical_findings.finding: The build process generates a single, large search index file for a moderately sized note collection. This results in a long initial load time, high memory usage, and unresponsive search UI on client devices, particularly on mobile or slow networks, failing the performance success criteria.

closure.closure_target: The search index strategy must support techniques for large collections, such as index sharding, lazy-loading of index segments, or using more compact data formats, to ensure the initial client-side payload remains small and the search UI is responsive quickly.
